name: Ottoman Empire
description: Designed in 1882 during Sultan Abdul Hamid II reign. Features the imperial tughra, scales of justice, the Quran, and 30 battle weapons surrounding the sun shield.

name: Soviet Union (USSR)
description: Adopted in 1923, depicting the hammer and sickle on a globe bathed in sun rays, framed by wheat stalks wrapped in ribbons carrying "Workers of the world, unite!" in 15 languages.

name: Austro-Hungarian Empire
description: The imperial double-headed eagle of the House of Habsburg-Lorraine, crowned with the Imperial Crown of Austria and bearing heraldic shields of the dual monarchy realms.

name: Russian Empire
description: The golden double-headed eagle of the Romanov dynasty, crowned with imperial crowns and displaying Saint George slaying the dragon on the breast shield.

name: Byzantine Empire
description: The imperial gold double-headed eagle of the Palaiologos dynasty on a crimson field, symbolizing dominance over both East and West.

name: German Empire (Deutsches Kaiserreich)
description: The Reichsadler (Imperial Eagle) bearing the Hohenzollern escutcheon, surrounded by the collar of the Order of the Black Eagle beneath the Imperial Crown.

name: Kingdom of Prussia
description: Features the crowned black eagle holding a royal scepter and orb, with the monogram of King Frederick I on its chest.

name: SFR Yugoslavia
description: Six torches burning in a single flame, symbolizing brotherhood and unity among the six constituent republics, topped by a red socialist star.

name: Holy Roman Empire
description: The black double-headed eagle on a golden banner with golden halos, representing universal Christian temporal authority.

name: Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
description: Quartered arms displaying the White Eagle of the Crown of Poland and the Vytis (Pahonia knight) of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania.

name: Empire of Brazil
description: Green escutcheon bordered with 20 stars surrounding the celestial sphere and the cross of the Order of Christ, flanked by coffee and tobacco branches.

name: Kingdom of Italy
description: The white cross on a red field of the royal House of Savoy, flanked by crowned lions and draped in the royal canopy.

name: United Kingdom
description: Supported by the English Lion and Scottish Unicorn, featuring the French mottoes "Honi soit qui mal y pense" and "Dieu et mon droit".

name: United States
description: The Great Seal featuring the bald eagle clutching an olive branch with 13 olives and 13 arrows, beneath the motto "E Pluribus Unum".

name: Germany
description: The Bundesadler (Federal Eagle), one of the oldest state symbols in the world, originating from the medieval Holy Roman emperors.

name: Spain
description: Combines the historic kingdoms of Castile, León, Aragon, Navarre, and Granada, flanked by the Pillars of Hercules with the motto "Plus Ultra".

name: Türkiye
description: The Presidential Seal of Türkiye featuring a 16-pointed sun surrounded by 16 five-pointed stars representing the 16 Great Turkic Empires in history.

name: France
description: Features the Roman lictor fasces (symbolizing justice and unity), an oak branch (permanence), and an olive branch (peace), bearing the monogram RF.

name: Italy
description: The national emblem featuring the Stella d'Italia (star of Italy) centered on a five-spoked cogwheel, flanked by olive and oak branches.

name: Japan
description: The Imperial Seal of Japan (Chrysanthemum Seal), a 16-petaled crest used by the Emperor of Japan and the Imperial family since the 12th century.

name: Australia
description: Supported by a red kangaroo and an emu (animals chosen because neither can move backwards easily, signifying progress), set against flowering golden wattle.

name: Canada
description: Proclaimed by King George V in 1921, incorporating symbols of England, Scotland, Ireland, and France with Canadian red maple leaves.

name: Mexico
description: Depicts an Aztec legend: a Mexican golden eagle perched on a prickly pear cactus devouring a rattlesnake, standing on an island in Lake Texcoco.

name: Sweden
description: The Greater Coat of Arms featuring the three golden crowns (Tre Kronor) and the Folkung lion, supported by two crowned heraldic lions.

name: India
description: An adaptation of the Lion Capital of Ashoka from 250 BCE at Sarnath, with four Asiatic lions standing back to back above the motto "Satyameva Jayate" (Truth Alone Triumphs).

name: South Africa
description: Adopted on Freedom Day 2000, displaying the secretary bird with outstretched wings, a rising sun, king protea, elephant tusks, and San rock art figures.

name: Egypt
description: The Eagle of Saladin, bearing on its breast an escutcheon with the vertical stripes of the national flag and gripping a scroll inscribed with the state name.

name: Brazil
description: Features a central five-pointed star surrounded by coffee and tobacco sprigs, bearing the Southern Cross constellation within a blue circle.

name: Argentina
description: Features the Sun of May rising above two shaking hands holding a pike topped by a red Phrygian cap of liberty, encircled by laurel wreaths.

name: Ireland
description: The golden Gaelic harp (Cláirseach or Harp of Brian Boru) with silver strings on a field of Saint Patrick's blue.

name: Ukraine
description: The Tryzub (Golden Trident), the historic seal of Grand Prince Volodymyr the Great of Kyivan Rus from the 10th century on a blue shield.

name: Netherlands
description: The Royal Arms featuring a crowned golden lion bearing a sword and arrows of the House of Orange-Nassau beneath the royal mantle with motto "Je Maintiendrai".

name: Belgium
description: The Brabant lion rampant on a black shield supported by two lions holding Belgian banners, with the royal motto "L'union fait la force".

name: Switzerland
description: The iconic free-standing bold white cross with arms of equal length on a red heraldic shield, unchanged since the Old Swiss Confederacy.

name: Austria
description: The black federal eagle wearing a mural crown (representing the middle class), holding a hammer (working class) and sickle (farmers), with broken chains on its feet symbolizing liberation.

name: Norway
description: One of the oldest state coats of arms in Europe (since 1280), depicting a golden lion rampant crowned and holding an axe with a silver blade.

name: Denmark
description: Three crowned blue lions passant gardant accompanied by nine red water lily hearts on a golden heraldic shield, dating back to King Canute VI in 1194.

name: Finland
description: A crowned lion on a red field trampling a Russian sabre with its hind paws while wielding an armored sword, surrounded by nine silver roses.

name: Portugal
description: The armillary sphere (symbolizing Portugal's Age of Discoveries) supporting a white shield with five blue quinas (shields) bordered by seven golden castles.

name: Greece
description: A blue escutcheon charged with a white Greek cross, completely surrounded by two laurel branches, representing victory and ancient Greek heritage.

name: Poland
description: The White Eagle (Orzeł Biały) with a golden beak and talons, wearing a golden crown on a red heraldic shield, dating to the Piast dynasty.

name: Iceland
description: Features the four legendary landvættir (protector spirits of Iceland): the bull (Griðungur), the eagle (Gammur), the dragon (Dreki), and the rock giant (Bergrisi).

name: Saudi Arabia
description: Two crossed scimitars beneath a green date palm tree, representing strength, sacrifice, vitality, and prosperity.

name: South Korea
description: Features the Taegeuk yin-yang symbol encircled by five petals of the Mugunghwa (Rose of Sharon, national flower of Korea) with a ribbon bearing the state name.
